## Description

Reloading a Relay-attached session whose pane has scrollback shows only the **first** lines of the history, not the latest ones. The visible symptom is a terminal that reattaches with an incomplete pane: the bootstrap's caret floor truncates written lines that live in tmux history above the visible screen.

The regression is on `staging` at `993125da9` and is independent of any #2469 change: it was introduced by the #2464 caret floor (`strip_trailing_blank_rows` with `keep_through_row`).

## Reproduction

`e2e/tests/browser/terminal-io.spec.ts:396` — `a reload re-observes the session without repainting history into it (Relay, #1490)`. The fixture paints twenty numbered lines into a pane whose client viewport is sixteen rows, then reloads three times. The buffer after reload ends at `REPAINT-initial-0016`; 0017–0020 were dropped.

## Evidence

- Base staging `993125da9`, full suite, run [40319329890](https://github.com/BestNathan/nession/actions/runs/40319329890): `unexpected: 1`, same test, same `REPAINT-initial-0020` failure over all three Playwright attempts.
- The base staging push E2E (run 40264532670) selected only `terminal-attach-bootstrap` and `terminal-consistency-faults`, so `terminal-io` had never run on this base before.
- Deterministic Rust witness: `a_bootstrap_trim_keeps_history_above_the_visible_pane` and the two bootstrap unit fixtures added with the fix.

## Cause

`strip_trailing_blank_rows(capture, Some(cursor_y))` treated the pane's zero-based cursor **row** as an index into the capture's newline-delimited lines. Two facts make that invalid:

1. `capture-pane -S -<history>` starts **above** the visible pane, so the capture has more lines than the pane has rows.
2. `capture-pane -J` joins a wrapped line into one logical line, so one capture line can cover several screen rows.

The floor therefore kept the capture's first `cursor_y + 1` lines and removed everything below — history inclusion and wrapping both shift the index.

## Fix Direction

- `TmuxOps::pane_cursor` reads `#{cursor_x} #{cursor_y} #{pane_height}` from one answer; the height is part of the same query so a resize between reads cannot describe a screen that never existed.
- `strip_trailing_blank_rows` keeps the ordinary trim of blank geometry and then appends the number of blank rows between the last written line and the cursor: `trailing_blank_rows - (pane_height - 1 - cursor_y)`. It never removes a written line.
- Witnesses: a twenty-line/sixteen-row real-tmux fixture, a history unit fixture, and a wrapped-line unit fixture. The existing #2464 caret test stays green.

## Success Criteria

- [x] SC-01 A capture that starts above the visible pane, and a capture containing a `-J`-joined wrapped line, both keep every written line when the cursor floor is applied; the real-tmux fixture with twenty lines in a sixteen-row pane keeps all twenty.
- [ ] SC-02 The selected `terminal-io` browser regression (`a reload re-observes the session without repainting history into it`) passes at the merged staging SHA for both Relay and P2P, with no truncated bootstrap history.

## Acceptance Plan

```yaml

  SC-01:
    when: merged
    branch: staging
    method: agent
  SC-02:
    when: merged
    branch: staging
    method: agent
```
